````math
## Appendix A Theoretical Analysis

### A.1 Analysis on Log-Error Bound

#### Notation.

We assume that a correct final step, $`y=z_{T}=1`$, implies all previous
steps are correct. Define the stepwise conditional probabilities
$`u_{t}\coloneqq\Pr(z_{t}=1\mid x\mathchar 59\relax z_{1}=1\mathchar 59\relax\ldots\mathchar 59\relax z_{t-1}=1)`$
for $`t\in[T]`$. By the chain rule and the assumption, the true reward
function,

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
f(x)=p(y=1\mid x)=p(z_{T}=1\mid x)=p(z_{1:T}=1\mid x)=\prod_{t=1}^{T}u_{t}(x)
``` |  |

and we write $`\zeta(x)\coloneqq\log f(x)=\sum_{t=1}^{T}\log u_{t}(x)`$.
For dPRM, we define the stepwise conditional distribution
$`\hat{u}_{t}(x)\coloneqq\hat{f}_{\textsf{dPRM}}(x_{1:t})`$ and use
product for the aggregation, i.e.,
$`\hat{f}_{\textsf{dPRM}}(x)\coloneqq\prod_{t=1}^{T}\hat{u}_{t}(x)`$.
Similarly, we define the conditional distribution
$`F_{t}(x\mathchar 59\relax v_{\leq t})\in[0\mathord{\mathchar 59\relax}1]`$
to be the gPRM’s normalized probability that step $`t`$ is correct given
the verification prefix,
i.e.$`\hat{f}_{\textsf{gPRM}}(x)\coloneqq\mathbb{E}_{v_{1:L^{+}}}[\prod_{t=1}^{T}F_{t}(x\mathchar 59\relax v_{\leq t})]`$.
To bound log probability, we assume there is
$`\varsigma\in(0\mathord{\mathchar 59\relax}1/2]`$ such that all
probabilities/predictors appearing inside logarithms are clipped into
$`[\varsigma\mathord{\mathchar 59\relax}1-\varsigma]`$. Hence all logs
are finite and $`\lvert\log(\cdot)\rvert\leq\log(1/\varsigma)`$.

#### Error terms.

1.  1.
    dPRM: Define $`\delta_{t}\coloneqq\log\hat{u}_{t}-\log u_{t}`$
    (evaluated at the appropriate prefixes), and

    |  |  |  |
    |----|----|----|
    |  |
    ``` math
    m_{t}\coloneqq\mathbb{E}[\delta_{t}\mid x]\mathchar 59\relax\quad\xi_{t}\coloneqq\delta_{t}-m_{t}\mathchar 59\relax
    ``` |  |

    so $`\mathbb{E}[\xi_{t}\mid x]=0`$.
2.  2.
    dORM or gORM: Let
    $`\epsilon\in\{\epsilon_{d}\mathord{\mathchar 59\relax}\epsilon_{g}\}`$,

    |  |  |  |
    |----|----|----|
    |  |
    ``` math
    \epsilon_{d}\coloneqq\log\hat{f}_{\textsf{dORM}}(x)-\log f(x)\mathchar 59\relax\quad\epsilon_{g}\coloneqq\log\hat{f}_{\textsf{gORM}}(x)-\log f(x)\mathchar 59\relax
    ``` |  |

    and decompose

    |  |  |  |
    |----|----|----|
    |  |
    ``` math
    \bar{m}\coloneqq\mathbb{E}[\epsilon\mid x]\mathord{\mathchar 59\relax}\quad\bar{\xi}\coloneqq\epsilon-\bar{m}\mathchar 59\relax\quad\beta_{\mathrm{orm}}^{2}\coloneqq\mathbb{E}[\bar{m}^{2}]\mathchar 59\relax
    ``` |  |

    so that $`\mathbb{E}[\bar{\xi}\mid x]=0`$.
3.  3.
    gPRM: For a single rollout
    $`v_{1:L^{+}}\sim p_{\textsf{gPRM}}(\cdot\mid x)`$, define

    |  |  |  |
    |----|----|----|
    |  |
    ``` math
    \tilde{u}_{t}\coloneqq F_{t}(x\mathord{\mathchar 59\relax}v_{\leq t})\mathchar 59\relax\quad\tilde{f}_{\textsf{gPRM}}(x)\coloneqq\prod_{t=1}^{T}\tilde{u}_{t}.
    ``` |  |

    The sampled gPRM log-error is

    |  |  |  |
    |----|----|----|
    |  |
    ``` math
    \Delta_{\textsf{gPRM}}~\coloneqq~\log\tilde{f}_{\textsf{gPRM}}(x)-\zeta(x)=\sum_{t=1}^{T}\delta_{t}^{(g)}\mathchar 59\relax\quad\delta_{t}^{(g)}\coloneqq\log\tilde{u}_{t}-\log u_{t}.
    ``` |  |

    Let

    |  |  |  |
    |----|----|----|
    |  |
    ``` math
    m_{t}^{(g)}\coloneqq\mathbb{E}[\delta_{t}^{(g)}\mid x]\mathchar 59\relax\quad\xi_{t}^{(g)}\coloneqq\delta_{t}^{(g)}-m_{t}^{(g)}\mathchar 59\relax
    ``` |  |

    so that $`\mathbb{E}[\xi_{t}^{(g)}\mid x]=0`$.

#### Assumptions.

There exist constants $`\sigma^{2}>0`$, $`\rho\geq 0`$, and an integer
$`k\geq 0`$ (independent of $`T`$) such that for all $`x`$,

1.  1.
    (Average variance floors)
    $`\frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=1}^{T}\mathrm{Var}(\xi_{t}\mid x)\geq\sigma^{2}`$,
    $`\frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=1}^{T}\mathrm{Var}(\xi_{t}^{(g)}\mid x)\ \geq\ \sigma^{2}+\tau^{2}`$.
2.  2.
    (Local error dependence) For any step $`s\mathchar 59\relax t`$,
    errors are only correlated within a local context window $`k`$, such
    that $`\mathrm{Cov}(\xi_{s}\mathchar 59\relax\xi_{t}\mid x)=0`$ for
    $`|s-t|>k`$. Within this window, the anti-correlation is bounded by
    $`\mathrm{Cov}(\xi_{s}\mathchar 59\relax\xi_{t}\mid x)\geq-\rho`$.
    (The same holds for $`\xi^{(g)}`$).
3.  3.
    (Positive slope) $`\sigma^{2}>2k\rho`$.

Unlike a strict per-step floor, the average variance condition naturally
accommodates deterministic or purely algebraic reasoning steps (where
variance is near zero), provided the cumulative chain injects a
proportional amount of noise. Similarly, the local dependence assumption
reflects bounded memory in autoregressive generation. While a model may
self-correct recent errors within a window $`k`$, distant steps become
conditionally independent. Notice that bounded local dependence implies
$`\sum_{1\leq s<t\leq T}\mathrm{Cov}(\xi_{s}\mathord{\mathchar 59\relax}\xi_{t}\mid x)\geq-k\rho T`$.

For gPRM with *sampled* verification CoTs, sampling contributes per-step
noise:
$`\frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=1}^{T}\mathrm{Var}(\xi_{t}^{(g)}\mid x)\geq\sigma^{2}+\tau^{2}`$
for some $`\tau^{2}>0`$. For ORMs, assume
$`\mathrm{Var}(\bar{\xi}\mid x)\leq\tau_{\mathrm{orm}}^{2}<\infty`$ (no
$`T`$-dependence).

###### Theorem A.1 (Log-error bound of dORM or gORM).

Let
$`\epsilon\in\{\epsilon_{d}\mathord{\mathchar 59\relax}\epsilon_{g}\}`$
and write $`\epsilon=\bar{m}+\bar{\xi}`$ with
$`\mathbb{E}[\bar{\xi}\mid x]=0`$. If
$`\mathrm{Var}(\bar{\xi}\mid x)\leq\tau_{\mathrm{orm}}^{2}`$
(independent of $`T`$), then

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\mathbb{E}[\epsilon^{2}]\ =\ \mathbb{E}[\mathrm{Var}(\bar{\xi}\mid x)]\;+\;\mathbb{E}[\bar{m}^{2}]\ \leq\ \tau_{\mathrm{orm}}^{2}\;+\;\beta_{\mathrm{orm}}^{2}\mathchar 59\relax
``` |  |

a bound that does not depend on the CoT length $`T`$.

###### Theorem A.2 (Log-error lower bound of dPRM).

Let
$`\Delta_{\textsf{dPRM}}\coloneqq\log\hat{f}_{\textsf{dPRM}}(x)-\zeta(x)`$.
Under the assumptions above,

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\mathbb{E}\big[\Delta_{\textsf{dPRM}}^{2}\big]\ \geq\ (\sigma^{2}-2k\rho)T.
``` |  |

###### Theorem A.3 (Log-error lower bound of gPRM).

Under the assumptions above,

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\mathbb{E}\!\big[\Delta_{\textsf{gPRM}}^{2}\big]~\geq~(\sigma^{2}+\tau^{2}-2k\rho)T.
``` |  |

#### Jensen-gap representation (mean predictor).

Let
$`L(x\mathord{\mathchar 59\relax}v)\coloneqq\sum_{t=1}^{T}\log F_{t}(x\mathord{\mathchar 59\relax}v_{\leq t})`$
and $`K_{x}(\theta)\coloneqq\log\mathbb{E}[e^{\theta L}\mid x]`$. Define
the mean predictor $`\mu(x)\coloneqq\mathbb{E}[e^{L}\mid x]`$ and
$`\Delta_{\mathrm{mean}}(x)\coloneqq\log\mu(x)-\zeta(x)`$. Then with
$`B^{(g)}(x)\coloneqq\mathbb{E}[L\mid x]-\zeta(x)`$, we have the exact
decomposition

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\Delta_{\mathrm{mean}}(x)=B^{(g)}(x)+\delta_{J}(x)\mathord{\mathchar 59\relax}\quad\delta_{J}(x)=K_{x}(1)-K_{x}^{\prime}(0)=\int_{0}^{1}(1-\theta)\,\mathrm{Var}_{\theta}(L\mid x)\,d\theta\geq 0\mathchar 59\relax
``` |  |

where $`\mathrm{Var}_{\theta}`$ denotes variance under the exponentially
tilted law $`d\mathbb{P}_{\theta}\propto e^{\theta L}d\mathbb{P}`$,
i.e.,
$`d\mathbb{P}_{\theta}(v)=\mathbbm{1}\{M(\theta)>0\}\,e^{\theta L(x\mathord{\mathchar 59\relax}v)}\,M(\theta)^{-1}d\mathbb{P}(v)`$
with $`M(\theta)\coloneqq\mathbb{E}[e^{\theta L}\mid x]`$.

###### Theorem A.4 (Log-error lower bound of mean-gPRM).

Assume the conditions of
Theorem [A.3](#A1.Thmthm3 "Theorem A.3 (Log-error lower bound of gPRM). ‣ Assumptions. ‣ A.1 Analysis on Log-Error Bound ‣ Appendix A Theoretical Analysis ‣ Rethinking Reward Models for Multi-Domain Test-Time Scaling").
In addition, suppose there exists
$`\kappa\in(0\mathord{\mathchar 59\relax}1]`$ such that for all
$`\theta\in[0\mathord{\mathchar 59\relax}1]`$,

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\mathrm{Var}_{\theta}(L\mid x)\ \geq\ \kappa\,\mathrm{Var}(L\mid x).
``` |  |

Then, for every $`x`$,

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\Delta_{\mathrm{mean}}(x)\ \geq\ B^{(g)}(x)\;+\;\frac{\kappa}{2}\,\mathrm{Var}(L\mid x)\ \geq\ B^{(g)}(x)\;+\;\frac{\kappa}{2}\Big((\sigma^{2}+\tau^{2}-2k\rho)T\Big).
``` |  |

Consequently,

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\mathbb{E}[\Delta_{\mathrm{mean}}]\ \geq\ \frac{\kappa}{2}\Big((\sigma^{2}+\tau^{2}-2k\rho)T\Big)\;-\;\sqrt{\mathbb{E}[B^{(g)}(x)^{2}]}\mathchar 59\relax\quad\mathbb{E}[\Delta_{\mathrm{mean}}^{2}]\ \geq\ \left(\max\{0\mathchar 59\relax\mathbb{E}[\Delta_{\mathrm{mean}}]\}\right)^{2}.
``` |  |

#### Takeaways.

Under mild anti-correlation and variance-floor assumptions, dPRM and
sampled gPRM incur log-error that grows at least linearly in the CoT
length $`T`$, and the additional sampling noise $`\tau^{2}`$ makes gPRM
strictly worse. In contrast, ORM estimators admit error bounds that are
independent of $`T`$ provided the conditional noise is bounded, which
makes them preferable for long CoTs. For mean-gPRM, the Jensen gap
introduces a strictly nonnegative bias that scales with the variance of
$`L`$ and hence with $`T`$, so even a calibrated predictor
($`B^{(g)}=0`$) exhibits error that increases with chain length. All
proofs are deferred
to [Section A.2](#A1.SS2 "A.2 Proofs ‣ Appendix A Theoretical Analysis ‣ Rethinking Reward Models for Multi-Domain Test-Time Scaling").

### A.2 Proofs

#### Proof of [Theorem A.1](#A1.Thmthm1 "Theorem A.1 (Log-error bound of dORM or gORM). ‣ Assumptions. ‣ A.1 Analysis on Log-Error Bound ‣ Appendix A Theoretical Analysis ‣ Rethinking Reward Models for Multi-Domain Test-Time Scaling")

###### Proof.

By the conditional bias–variance decomposition (law of total variance),

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\mathbb{E}[\epsilon^{2}]=\mathbb{E}\big[\mathrm{Var}(\epsilon\mid x)\big]+\mathbb{E}\big[(\mathbb{E}[\epsilon\mid x])^{2}\big]=\mathbb{E}\big[\mathrm{Var}(\bar{\xi}\mid x)\big]+\mathbb{E}\big[\bar{m}^{2}\big].
``` |  |

The assumption
$`\mathrm{Var}(\bar{\xi}\mid x)\leq\tau_{\mathrm{orm}}^{2}`$ for all
$`x`$ gives
$`\mathbb{E}[\mathrm{Var}(\bar{\xi}\mid x)]\leq\tau_{\mathrm{orm}}^{2}`$,
and by definition $`\beta_{\mathrm{orm}}^{2}=\mathbb{E}[\bar{m}^{2}]`$.
∎

#### Proof of [Theorem A.2](#A1.Thmthm2 "Theorem A.2 (Log-error lower bound of dPRM). ‣ Assumptions. ‣ A.1 Analysis on Log-Error Bound ‣ Appendix A Theoretical Analysis ‣ Rethinking Reward Models for Multi-Domain Test-Time Scaling").

###### Proof.

Let

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
B\coloneqq\sum_{t=1}^{T}m_{t}\mathord{\mathchar 59\relax}\qquad N\coloneqq\sum_{t=1}^{T}\xi_{t}\mathchar 59\relax
``` |  |

so $`\Delta_{\textsf{dPRM}}=B+N`$ with $`\mathbb{E}[N\mid x]=0`$. By the
tower property,

|  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|
|  | $`\displaystyle\mathbb{E}\!\left[\Delta_{\textsf{dPRM}}^{2}\right]`$ | $`\displaystyle=\mathbb{E}\!\big[\mathbb{E}[(B+N)^{2}\mid x]\big]=\mathbb{E}\!\big[B^{2}+2B\mathbb{E}[N\mid x]+\mathbb{E}[N^{2}\mid x]\big]`$ |  |
|  |  | $`\displaystyle=\mathbb{E}\!\big[\mathrm{Var}(N\mid x)\big]+\mathbb{E}[B^{2}]\ \geq\ \mathbb{E}\!\big[\mathrm{Var}(N\mid x)\big].`$ |  |

Expanding the variance yields:

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\mathrm{Var}(N\mid x)=\sum_{t=1}^{T}\mathrm{Var}(\xi_{t}\mid x)+2\!\!\sum_{1\leq s<t\leq T}\!\!\mathrm{Cov}(\xi_{s}\mathchar 59\relax\xi_{t}\mid x).
``` |  |

By local dependence,
$`\mathrm{Cov}(\xi_{s}\mathchar 59\relax\xi_{t}\mid x)=0`$ when
$`|s-t|>k`$. Hence only pairs with $`t-s\leq k`$ contribute. For each
$`t`$, there are at most $`k`$ indices $`s<t`$ with $`t-s\leq k`$, so
the number of contributing pairs is at most $`kT`$. Since each such
covariance is bounded below by $`-\rho`$, we have

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\sum_{1\leq s<t\leq T}\mathrm{Cov}(\xi_{s}\mathchar 59\relax\xi_{t}\mid x)\geq-k\rho T\mathchar 59\relax
``` |  |

and therefore $`2\sum_{s<t}\mathrm{Cov}(\cdot)\geq-2k\rho T`$. Combining
the variance floor and the covariance bound, for every fixed $`x`$,

|  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|
|  | $`\displaystyle\mathrm{Var}(N\mid x)`$ | $`\displaystyle=\sum_{t=1}^{T}\mathrm{Var}(\xi_{t}\mid x)+2\sum_{1\leq s<t\leq T}\mathrm{Cov}(\xi_{s}\mathord{\mathchar 59\relax}\xi_{t}\mid x)`$ |  |
|  |  | $`\displaystyle\geq\sum_{t=1}^{T}\mathrm{Var}(\xi_{t}\mid x)-2k\rho T`$ |  |
|  |  | $`\displaystyle\geq T\sigma^{2}-2k\rho T.`$ |  |

Taking expectations over $`x`$ preserves inequalities, so

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\mathbb{E}\big[\mathrm{Var}(N\mid x)\big]\ \geq\ \mathbb{E}\big[T\sigma^{2}-2k\rho T\big]=(\sigma^{2}-2k\rho)T.
``` |  |

Substituting back into the earlier bound
$`\mathbb{E}[\Delta_{\textsf{dPRM}}^{2}]\geq\mathbb{E}[\mathrm{Var}(N\mid x)]`$
yields

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\mathbb{E}\!\left[\Delta_{\textsf{dPRM}}^{2}\right]\ \geq\ (\sigma^{2}-2k\rho)T\mathchar 59\relax
``` |  |

as claimed. ∎

#### Proof of [Theorem A.3](#A1.Thmthm3 "Theorem A.3 (Log-error lower bound of gPRM). ‣ Assumptions. ‣ A.1 Analysis on Log-Error Bound ‣ Appendix A Theoretical Analysis ‣ Rethinking Reward Models for Multi-Domain Test-Time Scaling")

###### Proof.

Decompose

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\Delta_{\textsf{gPRM}}=\sum_{t=1}^{T}\delta_{t}^{(g)}=\underbrace{\sum_{t=1}^{T}m_{t}^{(g)}}_{\eqqcolon\,B^{(g)}}+\underbrace{\sum_{t=1}^{T}\xi_{t}^{(g)}}_{\eqqcolon\,N^{(g)}}.
``` |  |

Conditional mean-zero $`\mathbb{E}[N^{(g)}\mid x]=0`$ implies

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\mathbb{E}\!\left[(\Delta_{\textsf{gPRM}})^{2}\right]=\mathbb{E}\!\left[\mathrm{Var}\!\left(N^{(g)}\mid x\right)\right]+\mathbb{E}\!\left[(B^{(g)})^{2}\right]\ \geq\ \mathbb{E}\!\left[\mathrm{Var}\!\left(N^{(g)}\mid x\right)\right].
``` |  |

Now expand $`\mathrm{Var}(N^{(g)}\mid x)`$ using the average variance
floor and local error dependence:

|  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|
|  | $`\displaystyle\mathrm{Var}(N^{(g)}\mid x)`$ | $`\displaystyle=\sum_{t=1}^{T}\mathrm{Var}(\xi_{t}^{(g)}\mid x)+2\sum_{1\leq s<t\leq T}\mathrm{Cov}(\xi_{s}^{(g)}\mathord{\mathchar 59\relax}\xi_{t}^{(g)}\mid x)`$ |  |
|  |  | $`\displaystyle\geq T(\sigma^{2}+\tau^{2})-2k\rho T.`$ |  |

Taking expectations in $`x`$ gives the stated bound. ∎

#### Proof of [Theorem A.4](#A1.Thmthm4 "Theorem A.4 (Log-error lower bound of mean-gPRM). ‣ Jensen-gap representation (mean predictor). ‣ A.1 Analysis on Log-Error Bound ‣ Appendix A Theoretical Analysis ‣ Rethinking Reward Models for Multi-Domain Test-Time Scaling")

###### Proof.

1) Exponential tilting and log-mgf. Define
$`M(\theta)\coloneqq\mathbb{E}[e^{\theta L}\mid x]`$ and
$`K_{x}(\theta)\coloneqq\log M(\theta)`$. Since
$`e^{\theta L}\in(0\mathord{\mathchar 59\relax}1]`$ for
$`\theta\in[0\mathord{\mathchar 59\relax}1]`$ and
$`\mathbb{E}[|L|^{2}]<\infty`$, dominated convergence yields
$`M^{\prime}(\theta)=\mathbb{E}[Le^{\theta L}\mid x]`$ and
$`M^{\prime\prime}(\theta)=\mathbb{E}[L^{2}e^{\theta L}\mid x]`$. Let
$`d\mathbb{P}_{\theta}(C)\coloneqq e^{\theta L(x\mathord{\mathchar 59\relax}C)}M(\theta)^{-1}d\mathbb{P}(C)`$
and
$`\mathbb{E}_{\theta}[\cdot]\coloneqq\mathbb{E}[\cdot\,e^{\theta L}]/M(\theta)`$.
Then

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
K_{x}^{\prime}(\theta)=\frac{M^{\prime}(\theta)}{M(\theta)}=\mathbb{E}_{\theta}[L\mid x]\mathchar 59\relax\qquad K_{x}^{\prime\prime}(\theta)=\frac{M^{\prime\prime}(\theta)M(\theta)-(M^{\prime}(\theta))^{2}}{M(\theta)^{2}}=\mathrm{Var}_{\theta}(L\mid x).
``` |  |

2) Jensen-gap identity. Taylor with integral remainder at $`\theta=0`$
gives

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
K_{x}(1)=K_{x}(0)+K_{x}^{\prime}(0)+\int_{0}^{1}(1-\theta)K_{x}^{\prime\prime}(\theta)\,d\theta.
``` |  |

Since $`K_{x}(0)=0`$ and $`K_{x}^{\prime}(0)=\mathbb{E}[L\mid x]`$, we
obtain

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\log\mu(x)=\mathbb{E}[L\mid x]+\int_{0}^{1}(1-\theta)\,\mathrm{Var}_{\theta}(L\mid x)\,d\theta.
``` |  |

By definition of the mean predictor,

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\Delta_{\mathrm{mean}}(x)=\log\mu(x)-\zeta(x)\mathchar 59\relax\text{ where }\mu(x)=\mathbb{E}[e^{L}\mid x].
``` |  |

Plugging $`\log\mu(x)=\Delta_{\mathrm{mean}}(x)+\zeta(x)`$ with
$`B^{(g)}(x)\coloneqq\mathbb{E}[L\mid x]-\zeta(x)`$, this yields

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\Delta_{\mathrm{mean}}(x)=B^{(g)}(x)+\delta_{J}(x)\mathord{\mathchar 59\relax}\quad\delta_{J}(x)\coloneqq\int_{0}^{1}(1-\theta)\,\mathrm{Var}_{\theta}(L\mid x)\,d\theta\;\geq 0.
``` |  |

3) Lower bound on $`\delta_{J}`$ and variance linkage. By
tilt-stability,

|     |                                                           |     |
|-----|-----------------------------------------------------------|-----|
|     |
       ``` math
       \delta_{J}(x)\geq\frac{\kappa}{2}\,\mathrm{Var}(L\mid x).
       ```                                                        |     |

Moreover, since
$`L=\zeta(x)+\Delta_{\textsf{gPRM}}=\zeta(x)+B^{(g)}+N^{(g)}`$ with
$`\mathbb{E}[N^{(g)}\mid x]=0`$, and since $`\zeta(x)`$ and
$`B^{(g)}(x)`$ are constants when conditioning on $`x`$, we have

|     |                                                    |     |
|-----|----------------------------------------------------|-----|
|     |
       ``` math
       \mathrm{Var}(L\mid x)=\mathrm{Var}(N^{(g)}\mid x).
       ```                                                 |     |

Expanding and using the average variance floors and local error
dependence conditions (as in
Theorem [A.3](#A1.Thmthm3 "Theorem A.3 (Log-error lower bound of gPRM). ‣ Assumptions. ‣ A.1 Analysis on Log-Error Bound ‣ Appendix A Theoretical Analysis ‣ Rethinking Reward Models for Multi-Domain Test-Time Scaling")),

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\mathrm{Var}(N^{(g)}\mid x)\ \geq\ T(\sigma^{2}+\tau^{2})-2k\rho T.
``` |  |

Combining this gives the pointwise bound

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\Delta_{\mathrm{mean}}(x)\ \geq\ B^{(g)}(x)+\frac{\kappa}{2}\Big(T(\sigma^{2}+\tau^{2})-2k\rho T\Big).
``` |  |

4) Expectations and MSE. Taking expectations over $`x`$ and applying
Cauchy–Schwarz to $`\mathbb{E}[B^{(g)}(x)]`$ yields

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\mathbb{E}[\Delta_{\mathrm{mean}}]\ \geq\ \frac{\kappa}{2}\Big((\sigma^{2}+\tau^{2}-2k\rho)T\Big)-\sqrt{\mathbb{E}[B^{(g)}(x)^{2}]}.
``` |  |

Finally, Jensen’s inequality gives
$`\left(\max\{0\mathchar 59\relax\mathbb{E}[\Delta_{\mathrm{mean}}]\}\right)^{2}\leq\mathbb{E}[\Delta_{\mathrm{mean}}^{2}]`$,
so the MSE bound follows. In the calibrated case $`B^{(g)}\equiv 0`$,
the stated simplified bounds hold. ∎

## Appendix C Dataset

In this section, we provide more details on the datasets.

#### Math Datasets.

For the math domain, we use the widely adopted PRM800K ([Lightman
et al., 2024](#bib.bib31)) for training, where the process labels
$`z_{1:T}`$ are human-annotated. For training ORMs, we set the outcome
label $`y=\mathbbm{1}\!\big(z_{1:T}=\mathbf{1}_{T}\big)`$ (rather than
$`y=\mathbbm{1}(\hat{a}(r_{T})=a)`$), since PRM800K provides
high-quality ground-truth process labels. As a testbed, we use
[ProcessBench](https://huggingface.co/datasets/Qwen/ProcessBench) ([Zheng
et al., 2024](#bib.bib62)), which comprises four splits: 400 CoTs from
GSM8K ([Cobbe et al., 2021](#bib.bib7)), 1K from Math ([Hendrycks
et al., 2021](#bib.bib22)), 1K from Omni-Math ([Gao et al.,
2025](#bib.bib15)), and 1K from OlympiadBench ([He et al.,
2024](#bib.bib21)). We evaluate outcome verification by predicting
$`y\in\{0\mathord{\mathchar 59\relax}1\}`$ using the
final_answer_correct field. We also generate $`N=16`$ CoTs per question
with
[Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct) ([Qwen
Team, 2024a](#bib.bib37)) to assess test-time scaling (TTS).

Table 1: Dataset statistics for each domain of MMLU-pro ([Wang et al.,
2024c](#bib.bib50)). We report the number of questions, the number of
CoTs, and the average number of CoTs per question for both training and
test splits.

#### Multi-domain datasets.

For the multi-domain setting, we adopt MMLU-Pro ([Wang et al.,
2024c](#bib.bib50)), a 10-choice benchmark spanning 14 domains: law,
psychology, chemistry, biology, physics, history, economics, math,
business, philosophy, health, engineering, computer science, and other.
As shown in
[Table 1](#A3.T1 "In Math Datasets. ‣ Appendix C Dataset ‣ Rethinking Reward Models for Multi-Domain Test-Time Scaling"),
the corpus includes 5,750 training and 2,063 evaluation questions. For
each question, [Zeng et al. (2025)](#bib.bib58) generate 16/128 CoTs for
training/evaluation with
[Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct](https://huggingface.co/meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct) ([Dubey
et al., 2024](#bib.bib12)), and auto-label reasoning steps (i.e.,
process labels) using
[Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct](https://huggingface.co/meta-llama/Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct)
with prompts in
[Figs. 16](#A2.F16 "In Appendix B Prompts ‣ Rethinking Reward Models for Multi-Domain Test-Time Scaling")
and [17](#A2.F17 "Fig. 17 ‣ Appendix B Prompts ‣ Rethinking Reward Models for Multi-Domain Test-Time Scaling");
please see [Zeng et al. (2025)](#bib.bib58) for more details. To assess
generalization across CoTs from different $`p_{\mathtt{LLM}}`$, we also
generate 16 CoTs per evaluation question using
[SmolLM3-3B](https://huggingface.co/HuggingFaceTB/SmolLM3-3B) ([Bakouch
et al., 2025](#bib.bib4)),
[Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct),
[gemma-2-9b-it](https://huggingface.co/google/gemma-2-9b-it) ([Gemma
Team et al., 2024](#bib.bib16)), and
[Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct](https://huggingface.co/meta-llama/Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct),
spanning diverse model sizes and families.

## Appendix D Implementation Details

In this section, we provide implementation details omitted from the main
paper due to space limits.

#### Backbones for reward models.

Following [Zhang et al. (2025a)](#bib.bib59) and [Khalifa et al.
(2025)](#bib.bib27), we use
[R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B](https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B)
and
[R1-Distill-Qwen-7B](https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B) ([Guo
et al., 2025](#bib.bib20)) for the math domain, and
[R1-Distill-Llama-8B](https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B)
and
[R1-Distill-Qwen-14B](https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-14B)
for the multi-domain setting, as reward-model backbones. We also use
[Qwen3-8B](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3-8B) as the backbone to
assess whether the results hold for non-distilled backbones in the
multi-domain setting. Note that VersaPRM ([Zeng et al.,
2025](#bib.bib58)) originally used
[Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct](https://huggingface.co/meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct)
as the reward-model backbone for dPRM; for a fair comparison, we use
[R1-Distill
models](https://huggingface.co/collections/deepseek-ai/deepseek-r1-678e1e131c0169c0bc89728d)
and [Qwen3-8B](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3-8B) for both dORM and
dPRM.

|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|----|----|----|----|----|----|----|----|----|
| Method | LoRA |  |  | Training |  |  |  |  |  | Inference |  |  |
|  | Rank $`r`$ | $`\alpha`$ | Dropout $`p`$ | Batch | Optim. | Epochs | LR | Decay | Scheduler | Package | Temp. $`\tau`$ | $`M`$ |
| dORM & dPRM | 16 | 32 | 0.1 | 16 | AdamW | 1 | $`10^{-4}`$ | $`10^{-2}`$ | Cosine | - | - | - |
| gORM & gPRM | 32 | 16 | 0.1 | 16 | AdamW | 1 | $`10^{-4}`$ | $`10^{-2}`$ | Linear | vLLM | 0.6 | 10 or 16 |

Table 2: Summary of hyperparameters.

#### Hyperparameters.

We apply LoRA ([Hu et al., 2022](#bib.bib23)) for parameter-efficient
fine-tuning, optimize with AdamW ([Loshchilov & Hutter,
2019](#bib.bib33)), and use vLLM ([Kwon et al., 2023](#bib.bib30)) for
fast inference. At inference, we sample $`M{=}16`$ verification CoTs for
the math domain and $`M{=}10`$ for the multi-domain setting.
Hyperparameters are summarized in
[Table 2](#A4.T2 "In Backbones for reward models. ‣ Appendix D Implementation Details ‣ Rethinking Reward Models for Multi-Domain Test-Time Scaling"):
for dORM/dPRM we adopt those of [Zeng et al. (2025)](#bib.bib58), and
for gORM/gPRM we follow [Khalifa et al. (2025)](#bib.bib27). Note that
in preliminary experiments we set $`r{=}32`$ and $`\alpha{=}16`$ for
dORM/dPRM to compare fairly with gORM/gPRM (also using $`r{=}32`$ and
$`\alpha{=}16`$). However, we observed an overall performance
degradation (e.g., $`\approx`$2%), so we follow the settings of [Zeng
et al. (2025)](#bib.bib58). The hyperparameters in
[Table 2](#A4.T2 "In Backbones for reward models. ‣ Appendix D Implementation Details ‣ Rethinking Reward Models for Multi-Domain Test-Time Scaling")
are shared across all experiments and we do not perform exhaustive
tuning⁴⁴ 4 In
[Table 3](#A7.T3 "In Appendix G Additional Analysis ‣ Rethinking Reward Models for Multi-Domain Test-Time Scaling"),
we report the results of sweeps over the learning rate and LoRA rank for
dPRM/gPRM.. We report means over five independent runs, except for
experiments using
[R1-Distill-Llama-8B](https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B)
and [Qwen3-8B](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3-8B) reward backbones.

#### Verification CoTs for gORM and gPRM.

Following [Khalifa et al. (2025)](#bib.bib27), we sample 4 different
verification CoTs for each question $`q`$ and CoT $`r_{1:T}`$ pair in
the training dataset by prompting
[QwQ-32B](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/QwQ-32B) ([Qwen Team,
2025](#bib.bib39)) with temperature=0.6, top_k=20, top_p=0.95, and
min_p=0 using the formats in
[Figs. 18](#A2.F18 "In Appendix B Prompts ‣ Rethinking Reward Models for Multi-Domain Test-Time Scaling")
and [19](#A2.F19 "Fig. 19 ‣ Appendix B Prompts ‣ Rethinking Reward Models for Multi-Domain Test-Time Scaling").
Note that [Khalifa et al. (2025)](#bib.bib27) originally used
[QwQ-32B-Preview](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/QwQ-32B-Preview) ([Qwen
Team, 2024b](#bib.bib38)). In preliminary experiments, we found
[QwQ-32B](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/QwQ-32B) more likely to follow
instructions and produce more parsable verification CoTs (e.g., 1K vs.
7K for gPRM in the law domain), so we use
[QwQ-32B](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/QwQ-32B) throughout.

For the math domain we set category as math; for the multi-domain
setting we use $`\texttt{category}\in`${law, …, computer science} and
leave it blank for other. For additional benchmarks, such as
GPQA-diamond, MedQA, and LEXam, we also leave category blank. We discard
any verification CoT that (i) has unparsable labels; (ii) contains
Chinese characters; (iii) exceeds the token limit—4,096 for
math ([Khalifa et al., 2025](#bib.bib27)) or 8,192 for multi-domain; or
(iv) whose parsed labels are inconsistent with the targets (e.g., $`y`$
or $`z_{1:T}`$), corresponding to the *consensus filtering* in
[Section 2.2](#S2.SS2 "2.2 Reward Models ‣ 2 Background and Related Work ‣ Rethinking Reward Models for Multi-Domain Test-Time Scaling").
We also balance the counts of Yes/No examples. The resulting training
sets contain 34,286 CoTs for gORM and 35,666 CoTs for gPRM in the math
domain, and 171,780 (gORM) and 94,156 (gPRM) in the multi-domain
setting.
````
